cells.tense: The pen is in your hand and the direction is steady in you.
cells.ask: Point one thing you do today at what you actually mean, then stop for the day and let what you cleared stand.
cells.core:
Something ended and you're not arguing with it. You're in the room while it gets cleared, awake to it, and what you decide in the morning is still what you're doing at night. What you feel and what you do are pointed the same way, so effort doesn't need a reason to keep going.

The endings are moving at your pace for once, and the clearing holds because the effort behind it is the person actually doing it. Point one thing you do today at what you actually mean, then stop for the day and let what you cleared stand. That's the back half of this: you keep your effort tied to what's true, and whatever you want next gets ground to stand on.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is steady and you're still the one holding it.
cells.verb: keeping what you're doing pointed at what you actually mean

cells.tense: You are living past the ending, bracing for a room that isn't cleared yet.
cells.ask: Choose one thing still in the old room, decide today whether it comes with you, and write the decision down once.
cells.core:
You're gripping the wheel through a turn you haven't reached. The ending is settled in your mind and you're already driving the next stretch while this room is still being cleared, so talking about it comes out as pushing. You can feel ahead of your own timeline, and it isn't peace.

Effort pointed that far ahead is what makes the present feel like something to get through. Put the extra into sorting: choose one thing still in the old room, decide today whether it comes with you, and write the decision down once. That gathers your thinking into one place so the movement can start feeling like yours.

cells.tense: You are still standing in the doorway that closed behind you.
cells.ask: Say one thing that ended, out loud, and name what it gave you that you're keeping.
cells.core:
The furniture is out and you haven't moved. The ending happened — you can point at it — but your effort isn't aimed at anything now, because the last thing it was aimed at is over. The waiting feels like loyalty to what's gone.

When direction comes from what you feel rather than from bracing, it comes from what actually grew here, not from what you lost. Say one thing that ended, out loud, and name what it gave you that you're keeping. That's the yield of a change like this, and the part of you with effort still attached is the part that can say it. The current moves when you give the finished thing its due, not when you keep pushing on ground that's already clean.
cells.sheetLine: The ending happened and you're still in the doorway.
cells.verb: keeping what you're doing pointed at what you actually mean

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already clearing.
cells.ask: Say the ending you've been calling 'the situation', once, and say who decided it.
cells.core:
Going well here, this looks like naming an ending the day you feel it and letting the clearing follow from the name. Instead the room is emptying and you describe it like something happening on its own. Boxes go out, conversations stop, and someone folds the papers — and none of it has your voice on it. The clearing is underway; your part in it isn't said.

What you've been managing moved through your hands the whole time. Say the ending plainly, and make one small commitment to what's growing — a single container, tended today, opened again next week. That's what makes the cleared ground yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're clearing this. You haven't said it's yours.
cells.verb: keeping what you're doing pointed at what you actually mean

attempts.check: The record calls the medicine 'Fulfillment' — abundant vision realized — but that is the medicine LINE, not a result; the cell must never imply the partnership delivers satisfaction, only that it feeds on integration. A reader could reasonably say 'my momentum isn't peaceful at all,' and the ask (sit with what has ended) still works: it teaches that the body notices an ending before the story does. The sentence that serves the writer is the closing one in the Too Much core — 'Wait for the timing to come to you' — it performs a tone the house rewards rather than standing as the ask itself; that is what has been re-cut here.
